// Appendix A: Visual Development Log

DesignDevelopment

A chronological record of poster design work from May 2024 to April 2026. Spanning the pre-brand period, the Underbelly era & the full Haystack rebrand. Each entry notes a specific design decision or shift, showing how the practice developed across two years of active work.

Oskar Patalas  ·  Haystack Promotions  ·  Bristol  ·  2024-2026

01

25th May 2024

Early Work

Wolfgang Trio Headline — The Croft

The earliest poster in this collection. Live photography is already the main visual element, treated with halftone grain for a raw, printed feel. The eye illustration border on the left is a bit random but it works. Typography is bold & well-spaced. The instinct to combine photography with graphic elements is already there, even if the execution is still finding its feet.

// Entry 01 of 16

02

5th July 2024

Early Work

Copper Dog @ The Louisiana

One of the earliest show posters. Heavy distressed type, dark industrial palette, deliberately confrontational layout. The copy at the bottom is completely absurd (in a good way) & that irreverent tone ended up becoming a Haystack thing. Basic compared to later work but the personality is already there.

// Entry 02 of 16

03

18th July 2024

Underbelly Era

Underbelly Alt Night — 18th July

The glitch aesthetic shows up here for the first time. Digital noise & chromatic aberration in the corners, deliberately lo-fi & corrupted. The headline typography is the boldest so far. Punk & DIY energy is very much the vibe. Growing confidence in high-contrast layouts.

// Entry 03 of 16

04

19th September 2024

Underbelly Era

Underbelly Alt Night — 19th September

This is where the star motif first appears. It comes back in pretty much every iteration after this, which wasn't planned but became a recurring brand element. The green duotone marks the start of a more deliberate colour approach. Layout is more organised than previous posters. Progress.

// Entry 04 of 16

05

17th October 2024

Underbelly Era

Underbelly Alt Night — 17th October

Deer illustration, purple & green palette, serif type. A big shift from the glitch stuff. Surreal imagery in an alt/punk context shouldn't work but it does. The composition is more intentional here. Starting to think about posters as designed things rather than just assembled ones.

// Entry 05 of 16

06

21st November 2024

Underbelly Era

Underbelly Alt Night — 21st November

The ransom note typography shows up here for the first time. This was the design choice that carried forward most directly into Haystack. The QR code is actually integrated into the layout rather than just dropped in at the end. Small thing but it matters. Cleaner & more purposeful than anything before it.

// Entry 06 of 16

07

7th November 2024

Underbelly Era: Experimental Direction

Bad News First — The Old England

Formatted as a full newspaper front page. Fake columns, real news copy as texture, handwritten 'blah blah' scrawled over the top. Completely different to every other poster in this collection & that was the point. Shows a willingness to throw out the template & start from a concept instead.

// Entry 07 of 16

08

6th June 2025

Haystack Era: Brand Maturity

Steve Conte Solo UK Tour — Headline Show

The most professionally demanding brief in the portfolio. Designing for an internationally recognised touring artist means the poster has to work at a different level. Dark atmospheric photography, clean type hierarchy, 'Presented by Haystack Promotions Company' in the header. This one could sit alongside major label tour materials without looking out of place.

// Entry 08 of 16

09

7th June 2025

Haystack Era: Brand Maturity

Curbside Dayfest

Rough, confrontational, screen-print aesthetic. Aggressive red type, snarling dog in a star. 'For the Culture This One.' The Headfirst Bristol Editor's Pick it received confirmed the poster was communicating exactly what the show stood for. No ambiguity, no polish. Just exactly what it is.

// Entry 09 of 16

10

23rd October 2025

Haystack Era: Brand Maturity

Haystack Alt Night — 23rd October

Blurred atmospheric photography & elegant serif type. A complete tonal shift from the earlier Haystack work. Less clutter, more space. The big design lesson here was learning when to stop adding things. Restraint is harder than it sounds & this is the first poster where it actually worked.

// Entry 10 of 16

11

23rd November 2025

Haystack Era: Concept Posters

Snuff Headline — Golden Lion

Started as a video poster concept & evolved into this. Botanical illustration, decorative borders, warm cream palette. Nothing about it looks like a typical Haystack poster & that was the right call. The aesthetic fits the Italian Flower-Punk billing perfectly. Designing around the artist rather than the brand.

// Entry 11 of 16

12

27th November 2025

Haystack Era: Brand Maturity

Haystack Alt Night — 27th November

The star motif from September 2024 comes back here, now working alongside atmospheric photography. The ransom note type from the Underbelly era is still present but more refined. Earlier experiments absorbed into a coherent identity rather than abandoned. The brand has memory.

// Entry 12 of 16

13

19th February 2026

Haystack Era: Recent Work

Haystack Alt Night — 19th February

A softer direction. Pastel halftone, script type, mixed typefaces. Testing what Haystack looks like outside of the dark punk aesthetic. Not every experiment sticks but that's kind of the point. Worth exploring even if it doesn't become the house style.

// Entry 13 of 16

14

5th March 2026

Haystack Era: Recent Work

Husk — Haystack Alt Night

Part of the ongoing exploration of what Haystack can look like beyond the established templates. The practice is still actively developing rather than repeating what already works. Each show is treated as an opportunity to try something different.

// Entry 14 of 16

15

19th March 2026

Haystack Era: Recent Work

Haystack Alt Night — 19th March

Collage aesthetic, surrealist imagery (horse, stacked televisions, a kid reading), red & cream palette, vertical text on the spine. Heavily influenced by post-punk record sleeve design. One of the most conceptually ambitious posters in the whole collection & probably the most fun to make.

// Entry 15 of 16

16

29th April 2026

Haystack Era: Latest Work

Break for Lovers Headline — The Croft

Vintage Hollywood film poster. Tagline, Technicolor credit, 'Directed by Haystack.' Deep red illustrated portrait. Nothing about it looks like a Bristol gig poster & that's the whole point. Comparing this to the Wolfgang Trio poster from two years earlier shows exactly how far the design practice has come.
